case_studies.title: Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs
case_studies.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) for training LLMs typically rely on ground-truth answers to assign rewards, limiting their applicability to tasks where the ground-truth solution is unknown. We introduce a \textbf{R}anking-\textbf{i}nduced \textbf{VER}ifiable framework (RiVER) that trains LLMs on score-based optimization tasks without ground-truth solutions, using deterministic execution feedback as continuous-valued supervision. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of training large language models (LLMs) without knowing the correct answers, by introducing a new framework called RiVER that uses score-based optimization tasks. The researchers built a framework that trains LLMs using deterministic execution feedback as supervision. The result is a more flexible way to train LLMs, but it's not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: When Does Combining Language Models Help? A Co-Failure Ceiling on Routing, Voting, and Mixture-of-Agents Across 67 Frontier Models
case_studies.abstract: Multi-model LLM systems such as routing, voting, cascades, fusion, and mixture-of-agents are used to beat single-model accuracy. We show that their gain is capped by a quantity the field rarely reports. For any policy whose output is one member model answer, accuracy cannot exceed one minus beta, where beta is the rate at which every model is wrong on the same query. In contrast, the usual diagnostic, average pairwise error correlation rho, cannot identify beta: error laws with identical marginals and pairwise correlations can have different all-wrong rates. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited accuracy in multi-model language systems by identifying a ceiling for their performance, known as the co-failure ceiling. The authors built a framework to measure this ceiling, which is the rate at which all models are wrong on the same query. The result shows that this ceiling limits the accuracy of these systems, regardless of their complexity.

case_studies.title: Prompt Injection in Automated Résumé Screening with Large Language Models: Single and Multi-Injection Settings
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to screen and rank job applicants, creating incentives for candidates to strategically manipulate algorithmic hiring systems. We study prompt injection in automated résumé screening, defined as subtle self-promotional text that introduces no new qualifications but is designed to influence LLM evaluations. Using controlled experiments, we show that prompt injection reliably improves applicant rankings when résumé quality is homogeneous and few candidates inject. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of how candidates can manipulate automated résumé screening systems using large language models. The researchers built experiments to test the effectiveness of 'prompt injection', which is adding self-promotional text to influence rankings. The result showed that prompt injection can improve rankings, but its effectiveness decreases as more candidates use it.

case_studies.title: Adaptive Utility driven Resource Orchestration for Resilient AI (AURORA-AI)
case_studies.abstract: Modern AI systems are increasingly deployed under non-stationary computational, demographic, and operational conditions in which static resource allocation strategies degrade both predictive performance and human-centric properties such as fairness and explainability. case_studies.summary: AURORA-AI solves the problem of static resource allocation in AI systems under changing conditions by continuously redistributing computational resources to improve predictive performance and fairness. The researchers built a framework that unifies feedback control, stability monitoring, and fairness-aware utility. The result is a more resilient AI system that adapts to non-stationary conditions.

case_studies.title: CHIA: An open-source framework for principled, agentic AI-driven hardware/software co-design research
case_studies.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence shows great promise for radically improving the pace of innovation in hardware/software co-design research across computer architecture, systems, compilers, and VLSI. Thus far, however, applications of AI in these contexts have generally been demonstrated in isolated settings on small-scale problems, due to the difficulty of designing and deploying complex AI-infused hardware and software development workflows. This paper introduces CHIA, an open-source hardware/software co-design framework for agile and principled research on the application of AI to co-design.
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of applying artificial intelligence to hardware and software design by introducing an open-source framework called CHIA. The authors built CHIA to enable agile and principled research on AI-driven hardware and software co-design. The result is a tool that can help improve the pace of innovation in computer architecture, systems, compilers, and VLSI.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it's focused on hardware and software design research rather than cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: Resource-Aware Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Local Small Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Small language models can run locally on consumer hardware, but structured reasoning often pushes users toward repeated sampling or larger models. This article studies a bounded neuro-symbolic alternative for local inference: a model translates a problem into typed finite-domain rules and constraints, a symbolic layer checks traceability and consistency, and a deterministic solver performs the reasoning step. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient reasoning in small language models by building a neuro-symbolic pipeline that combines symbolic and deterministic reasoning, resulting in more accurate and consistent outputs. The pipeline, called VFR-LLM, allows for local inference on consumer hardware without requiring repeated sampling or larger models. This improves the overall efficiency of language models in resource-constrained environments.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving language model reasoning on local hardware, but IT consultants working with AI models may be interested in this development for potential future applications.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Some novelty in exploring local small language models, but not directly applicable to current IT infrastructure. Potential for minor real-world impact, but not yet ready for practical use in IT. AI maturity is basic. No clear monetisation potential.

case_studies.title: Beyond Feedforward Networks: Reentry Neural Systems as the Fundamental Basis of Subjecthood and Intrinsic Safety of Next-Generation AGI

The system has a structural cycle that guarantees the emergence of a self-model, and the agent's goals are encoded in the architecture itself.
